data.one_liner: A drop-in ChangeNotifier replacement for observing specific model properties.
data.what_it_does: Extends ChangeNotifier to allow notifying listeners about specific property changes instead of an all-or-none approach. Provides PropertyChangeProvider and PropertyChangeConsumer widgets to rebuild descendants only when specific properties change.
use_when: You want a granular alternative to standard ChangeNotifier without learning a massive state management framework.
Your models are relatively simple and you want widgets to rebuild only when specific properties change.
avoid_when: You are already using a comprehensive state management framework like Riverpod or BLoC.
You need complex dependency injection and stream-based business logic separation.
strengths: 100% backwards compatible with existing ChangeNotifier code.
Supports fine-grained rebuilds based on specific property names.
Includes helper widgets like PropertyChangeProvider and PropertyChangeConsumer.
weaknesses: Relies on string literals or enums for property names, which can be less robust than fully typed states.
Not suitable for large-scale architectures requiring strict unidirectional data flow.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want standard inherited widget-based dependency injection and state management without property-level granularity.

alternatives.name: flutter_riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a robust, compile-safe, modern state management solution that avoids BuildContext.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a predictable, event-driven state management pattern.
